A-aperture-commerce.expect: Service readiness for payments-api; Alex assesses, Jordan validates, Maya coordinates; commercial details hidden from developers

sources.label: CRM record
sources.text:
Account: Aperture Commerce (FICTIONAL). Enterprise commerce and payments infrastructure.
Employees: 6,800. Engineers: 1,350 across 94 teams; roughly 720 services.
Opportunity: Portal Enterprise, potential $300K ARR. 60-day evaluation, stage: technical validation.
Champion: Maya Chen, Director of Platform Engineering. Account owner: Chris (us).

sources.label: Discovery call
sources.text:
[00:03] Maya Chen: Our biggest pain is that nobody can tell who owns a service. Ownership is all over the place and the runbooks are inconsistent or missing.
[00:07] Maya Chen: For the pilot let's use payments-api. It's on GitHub, but I'm honestly not sure the catalog file is up to date.
[00:10] Maya Chen: Alex Rivera can do the initial repository readiness assessment. Jordan Lee should independently check whether people can actually find the service and its docs.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Our VP thinks Backstage is a nice-to-have, so we need something concrete in 60 days.

sources.label: My notes
sources.text: Maya is the right champion. Don't share pricing or the VP comment with engineers. Not clear whether payments-api deploys with GitHub Actions or Jenkins - Maya said Actions, the SRE in the call said Jenkins.

B-cicd-standardization.expect: CI/CD assessment of pipeline inconsistency; pipeline-specific milestones; no catalog checklist

sources.label: Call with platform lead
sources.text:
Priya Nair (Platform Lead, Lumenfield Logistics, FICTIONAL): every team builds its own deployment pipeline. Some use GitHub Actions, two teams still run Jenkins, and the mobile team deploys by hand on Fridays.
Priya Nair: Releases fail differently in every team and we can't tell whether tests ran before a deploy. We want one standard pipeline template.
Priya Nair: Sam Okoro on the routing-service team is willing to be the first team to try it.

sources.label: Requirements
sources.text: Must keep existing AWS deploy targets. Pipelines must run unit tests and a security scan before deploy. Secrets currently live in each repo's CI settings.

C-developer-self-service.expect: Environment provisioning investigation with prerequisites and verification; no service-catalog milestone

sources.label: Discovery call
sources.text:
Lena Fischer (Engineering Manager, Quarry Health, FICTIONAL): it takes about two weeks to get a new test environment. Developers file a ticket, then ops builds it by hand with Terraform.
Lena Fischer: Teams end up sharing one staging environment and stepping on each other.
Lena Fischer: Tomas from the ops team owns the Terraform modules. Our developer Aisha Khan has volunteered to test a self-service flow.

sources.label: CRM
sources.text: Quarry Health, 900 employees. Deal: $85K, stage 2. Procurement needs SOC 2 report.

D-minimal-context.expect: Clarification questions only; no invented infrastructure, repositories or assignments

sources.label: Note
sources.text: We want better developer productivity and faster onboarding.
